# Test data: fixture policy, manifest and golden files

Status: current as of M5 (2026-10-22). This file is the authoritative inventory
and policy for everything under `testdata/`. All GenBank fixtures (5.1) and
SnapGene fixtures (5.2) are committed with recorded origin, licence and sha256,
and the reader/golden gate asserts their expected outcomes in CI. Rows move
`pending` -> `committed` -> `verified` as recorded in the status columns.

Authority order for fixture expectations:

1. `development-plan.md` section 7 (fixture matrices, golden rules, SnapGene
   ground truth) and the settled decisions in section 2 (D1-D16, S1-S9);
2. this file (policy, inventory, review process);
3. adapter design notes for format facts.

If a row here disagrees with the plan, the plan wins and this file must be
corrected in the same change. Fixture bytes never define semantics: the
canonical model documents do.

## 1. Directory layout

```text
testdata/
├── README.md          committed   this policy, manifest and known differences
├── genbank/           committed   synthetic GenBank .gb fixtures
├── snapgene/          committed   synthetic SnapGene .dna fixtures
├── expected/          committed   canonical JSON goldens
├── paired/            LOCAL ONLY  .dna + SnapGene "Save As" .gb (never committed)
└── corpus-local/      LOCAL ONLY  de-identified real corpus (never committed)
```

| Path | Committed | Contents | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `testdata/README.md` | yes | policy, fixture manifest, known-differences register | updated with every fixture change |
| `testdata/genbank/` | yes | `.gb` fixtures from the section 5.1 manifest | synthetic or self-built only |
| `testdata/snapgene/` | yes | `.dna` fixtures from the section 5.2 manifest | synthetic or self-built only; generated by our own deterministic container builder, never saved from SnapGene |
| `testdata/expected/` | yes | normalized canonical JSON goldens (`.json`) | one golden per successful import (see section 6) |
| `testdata/paired/` | no | `<stem>.dna`, `<stem>.gb`, `manifest.local.md` | local-only ground truth per open question Q8; gitignored |
| `testdata/corpus-local/` | no | de-identified real-world regression corpus | local-only; enabled through `SEQUON_CORPUS_DIR`; gitignored |

Rules for the tree:

- No other subdirectories and no archive containers (`.zip`, `.gz`, `.tar`,
  base64 blobs). A fixture is a single plain file.
- Do not copy local files into the committed tree to "make CI reproduce a bug".
  Reduce the input to a synthetic reproducer and record it as a matrix row.
- Generated reports (comparison output, diffs) belong under `target/` and are
  never committed.
- The digest vectors live at `tests/digest-vectors.json` (repository root, see
  section 7), not under `testdata/`.

## 2. Source, licence and de-identification policy

### 2.1 What may be committed

Only fixtures that are **synthetic or self-built**:

- hand-written text fixtures (small GenBank records, hostile-input stubs);
- files produced by a deterministic in-repository generator or test builder,
  whose generator path and version are recorded in the manifest;
- sequences/features composed by us for test coverage, including synthetic
  plasmid constructs.

Explicitly not allowed in the committed tree:

- any user, customer, patient or collaborator sequence, even "just the
  backbone", even de-identified;
- files downloaded from Addgene, NCBI, vendors or publication supplements;
  redistribution is not implied by public availability, and third-party terms
  are out of scope for this repository;
- files produced by SnapGene or another commercial sequence editor, including
  its GenBank exports (open question Q8; see section 8). Those stay in
  `testdata/paired/`;
- real sample identifiers, personal names, author/contact fields, institution
  names or free-text lab notes in headers, comments or qualifiers;
- secrets or machine-specific paths in fixture text (same rule as all
  repository text).

Real-world data is regression-only, stays local, and is read from
`SEQUON_CORPUS_DIR` (section 3). Tests must pass with the variable unset.

### 2.2 Provenance record for every committed fixture

Every committed fixture has one manifest row (section 5) with:

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| path | repository-relative path |
| sha256 | full lowercase hex digest of the final committed bytes |
| origin | `self-authored` or `generated: <generator path/name>`; the SnapGene set records `generated: dna_builder`, whose source is `crates/sequon-conformance/src/dna_builder.rs` |
| licence | `MIT (repository licence)`; if any third-party text is included, its licence as well |
| de-identification | `synthetic; no personal data` or the concrete transformation applied |
| date | date the final bytes were produced |
| status | `pending` -> `committed` -> `verified` (section 5 legend) |

Rules:

- The sha256 is recomputed whenever fixture bytes change; a recorded digest
  that does not match the file is a test failure, not a note.
- Generated fixtures must be reproducible: the generator is deterministic and
  committed (or its exact inputs and steps are documented in this file).
  Binary fixtures are never "edited by hand in a hex editor" without recording
  the edit.
- If a fixture must contain a GenBank header line (for header-preservation
  coverage), write neutral synthetic values; do not paste a real record header.

### 2.3 De-identification (local corpora only)

Anything that reaches `testdata/paired/` or `testdata/corpus-local/` is
reviewed before use:

1. strip COMMENT, REFERENCE, author/contact, institution and sample metadata;
2. replace names with synthetic identifiers (`sequon-test-001`, ...);
3. keep only fields a test asserts on; remove unrelated free text;
4. record what was removed/changed in the local manifest;
5. never commit the original or a diff containing it.

### 2.4 Licensing

The workspace is MIT. Fixture bytes authored here are covered by the
repository licence. Do not add a fixture that would require a different
licence, attribution notice or redistribution condition; if the only way to
cover a case is such a file, the case goes to `corpus-local/` or a synthetic
reproducer is built instead.

## 3. Local-only inputs

### 3.1 `testdata/paired/` (Q8)

Paired fixtures are the SnapGene ground truth: the same molecule as
`<stem>.dna` plus the vendor's `File -> Save As -> GenBank` export
`<stem>.gb`. Open question Q8 is not closed, so neither file is committed.
Both are gitignored. The directory is created on demand by a developer
following section 8, and `paired/manifest.local.md` records the SnapGene
version, OS, date and both sha256 values. It is also local-only. The
directory is ignored by the repository (`/testdata/paired/` in `.gitignore`):
Q8 leaves vendor-output redistribution unsettled, so nothing here may be
committed.

### 3.2 `testdata/corpus-local/` and `SEQUON_CORPUS_DIR`

- `SEQUON_CORPUS_DIR` points at a directory of de-identified real inputs,
  preserving the file extensions the adapters accept.
- When unset, corpus tests report a skip (never a failure); committed fixtures
  and goldens must be sufficient for CI.
- When set, the harness runs every corpus file, writes a report under
  `target/corpus/`, and fails on panics, unexpected error codes or golden
  mismatches for files that have committed expectations.
- The directory is ignored by the repository
  (`/testdata/corpus-local/` in `.gitignore`); it is never a CI input.
- Corpus content is never copied into `testdata/genbank/` or
  `testdata/snapgene/`, and corpus reports are never committed.

## 4. Naming conventions

- GenBank fixtures: `testdata/genbank/<NNN>-<kebab-slug>.gb`.
  Prefix `NNN` is the number from plan section 7.2; slug is lowercase ASCII
  with hyphens. Only the `.gb` extension is used in-repo. (Parsers still
  accept `.gbk`/`.genbank`; a fixture exercising that is only added with an
  explicit matrix row.)
- SnapGene fixtures: `testdata/snapgene/<NNN>-<kebab-slug>.dna`.
- Goldens: `testdata/expected/<fixture-stem>.json`, for example
  `testdata/expected/010-circular-plasmid.json`. The fixture stem is the file
  name without its extension; never reuse a stem across formats.
- Paired (local): `testdata/paired/<stem>.dna`, `<stem>.gb`,
  `manifest.local.md`.
- Corpus (local): opaque synthetic directory and file names; no customer,
  project or person names, even abbreviated.
- Do not renumber existing fixtures or reuse a number for a different case;
  append new rows to a group and update this file.

Number groups:

| Range | GenBank | SnapGene |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `00x` | minimal successful records | container/sequence basics |
| `01x`- `02x` | circular, location forms, partials, qualifiers | history versions, multi-segment features |
| `03x`- `06x` | unknown keys, multi-record, length mismatch, CRLF, no features | primers, notes/properties, traces, unknown packets |
| `07x`- `09x` | malformed/unsupported input | truncated, decompression bomb, deep XML |
| `1xx` | line endings, unterminated, unsupported molecule, hostile input, large file | unicode, duplicate/missing DNA packet |
| `13x`/ `16x` | required-field and molecule-type cases | sequence type and topology cases |

## 5. Fixture manifest

Status legend:

- `pending` - the reader/golden gate has not verified this row yet. A
  committed file may already be byte-final with a recorded sha256, but the M4
  importer has not asserted its expected outcome.
- `verified` - the reader imports the fixture and the expected outcome
  (success fields or diagnostic code) is asserted in CI.
- `variant-tested` (section 5.3 only) - the code has no code-string emission;
  the behavior is covered by a typed-error variant assertion instead.
- `reserved` (section 5.3 only) - the code is registered in diagnostics.md but
  not emitted by the current implementation: either a deliberately unreachable
  path or a deferred error path with no known input construction.

A row is `pending` at fixture-commit time; the `origin / licence` and
`sha256` columns become authoritative once the file exists (a missing or
stale sha256 is a test failure, see section 6.3). The `Expected` column is the
plan's expectation; where a diagnostic code is named, the test asserts that
code (and the record remains usable only when the plan says it does).

### 5.2 SnapGene fixtures (plan section 7.3)

These are synthetic containers generated by
`crates/sequon-conformance/src/dna_builder.rs`; none may be saved from
SnapGene and no corpus byte is copied. The byte-determinism gate is
`crates/sequon-conformance/tests/snapgene_fixtures.rs`: it rebuilds every file,
compares the committed bytes, the sha256 recorded in the tables below and an
independent container walk. Regenerating a fixture is a deliberate change made
with `cargo run -p sequon-conformance --bin gen-snapgene-fixtures`, followed by
reviewing the new sha256.

Construction status: types 0/3/5 (empty)/6/8/10/13 follow the corpus-verified
layout. Type 1 (2-bit), non-empty type 5 (030), history framing and the type
3/13 semantics are builder conventions that pin a reader interpretation; they
do not confirm the format fact (F-8..F-11, F-17, F-20, F-27). 080 uses the
LZMA-alone declared-size pre-check because `lzma-rs` 0.3.0 compresses repeated
input at roughly 40:1, below the 200:1 ratio cap, so a ratio-only bomb is not
constructible; the reader must reject the 13-byte header before decoding. 131
follows the strict lead decision: only sequence type 1 is DNA, any other value
is `DNA_UNKNOWN_SEQ_TYPE`, and `DNA_UNSUPPORTED_MOLECULE` stays reserved until
a real non-DNA file verifies the enum. 063 and 064 add the M4-requested type 17
alignable-sequences and type 29 history-modifier blocks with synthetic,
unverified XML shapes; both are preserved and reported, never interpreted. 133
has no known file construction and stays a unit-test trigger. Every fixture
whose golden or typed-error gate exists reads `verified`; 133 remains
`pending` because its bytes and expected outcome are not yet constructed.

### 5.3 Error-path coverage register (diagnostics.md and plan section 7.6)

Plan section 7.6 requires every diagnostic code to have a fixture **or** a
unit/integration test. The committed fixture set (20 GenBank rows, 19 plan
SnapGene rows and 13 additive SnapGene fixtures, 31 `.dna` files) covers 22 of
the 65 codes in the frozen vocabulary (`docs/design/diagnostics.md`).
`133-missing-topology.dna` remains a unit-test trigger because no known
container construction yields the required flag state, and
`DNA_UNSUPPORTED_MOLECULE` stays in the register because the strict lead
decision maps every non-1 sequence type to `DNA_UNKNOWN_SEQ_TYPE` until a real
non-DNA file verifies the enum. The remaining 43 codes are exercised by
focused tests over inline byte builders. A case may be promoted to a committed
fixture later, but only with a row in section 5 and lead approval; propose the
name here first.

Codes covered by fixtures: `GB_RECORD_UNTERMINATED` (120),
`GB_UNSUPPORTED_MOLECULE` (130), `GB_TOPOLOGY_MISSING` (161),

`unsupported_location`, `coordinate_out_of_range`, `malformed_metadata`

`DNA_FEATURE_MALFORMED`) and `not_requested` (the caller set
`preserve_unhandled_blocks = false`, so the block was fingerprinted instead of
kept; paired with the block's diagnostic, if any). New reasons are added to
diagnostics.md and here together, and adapter tests enforce the spelling and
the `what`/`reason` pairing.

## 6. Golden files and determinism

### 6.1 What a golden is

Goldens are the **normalized canonical JSON text** of imported records,
serialized through the canonical JSON profile
(`docs/design/canonical-json-profile.md`): fixed field order, fixed escaping,
fixed number format, LF line endings and a trailing newline. The golden is the
exact byte sequence CI compares; parsed-value comparison alone would not catch
field-order or escaping regressions.

Naming (lead decision, T3):

- single-record fixture: `testdata/expected/<fixture-stem>.json`;
- multi-record fixture: one golden per returned record,
  `testdata/expected/<fixture-stem>.<record-index>.json`, where the 0-based
  index matches `records[].index` in the import report;
- there is no bundle document and no bundle schema: a golden is always one
  record.

Content rules:

- Goldens are generated by the importer, never hand-copied from writer output
  (that would confirm the writer against itself).
- Error fixtures have no golden. Their tests assert the typed error variant,
  the diagnostic code, the position field and that no partial record is
  returned.
- Warning fixtures have a record golden plus structural diagnostics
  assertions in the test. **v1 has no import-report goldens** (lead decision,
  T4): tests assert `code`, `severity`, `position` and `record_index`, and
  never assert message text, so the frozen code vocabulary is not coupled to
  prose. Double-parse report equality is still tested for ordering.
- Serialized records use the `.json` extension; no alternate container.

### 6.2 Comparison and review

- Prefer direct byte comparison with the golden file. If snapshot testing is
  adopted for a suite, snapshots point at these same files and CI runs the
  check mode only.
- Diffs are human-reviewed and never auto-accepted. Do not run snapshot-update
  or rewrite modes in CI or in scripts; an update is a deliberate, reviewed
  commit that explains why the output changed.
- A changed canonical digest is a semantic identity change: it is only allowed
  together with a new digest algorithm id or a documented contract change
  (D4/D5), never as an incidental golden refresh.
- A golden diff must be reviewed by the author and one reviewer (plan section
  8.4), and the commit message must state the cause.
- Diagnostics are compared structurally (code, severity, position,
  record_index) and never by message text; two parses of the same bytes must
  still produce the same report order.

### 6.3 Determinism rules (asserted for every successful fixture)

1. Import the same bytes twice in one process and serialize both records:
   byte-identical output for the same crate version.
2. `write_genbank` twice for the same record: byte-identical output. No clock,
   locale or environment dependence; the default date is the fixed
   `01-JAN-2000` unless `WriteOptions.date` is set.
3. `import -> write_genbank -> import`: records deep-equal when `provenance`
   is ignored (plan section 7.4). Anything else that must be excluded is a
   contract change, not a test waiver.
4. Diagnostics are sorted by `(position.offset, code)`, so two parses of the
   same bytes produce the same report order.
5. `testdata/` is checked out byte-identically on every platform: LF-only
   files, no line-ending conversion, no BOM.
6. Goldens are verified on Linux CI and locally on macOS (plan section 7.4);
   a platform-dependent diff is a defect in the serializer, not a golden to
   update.
7. Every committed `.dna` fixture regenerates byte-identically from
   `crates/sequon-conformance/src/snapgene_fixtures.rs`, and the sha256 in
   section 5.2/5.2.1 matches the rebuilt bytes. The gate is
   `cargo test -p sequon-conformance --test snapgene_fixtures`; regenerating a
   fixture is a deliberate reviewed change, never an automatic update.

### 6.4 SnapGene golden gate (M4)

`testdata/expected/<fixture-stem>.json` now exists for every successful
SnapGene fixture (23 files: the 10 successful plan rows, the 11 calibration
additions, and 063/064).
Each golden is the canonical JSON text defined in section 6.1, produced by
importing the committed fixture with the committed `sequon-io` snapgene
reader, running `Record::validate()` and `sequon_algo::verify_digests()`, and
serializing through the canonical JSON module. Goldens were reviewed against
the accepted design note (fields, 0-based half-open coordinates, extras,
provenance) before being committed; canonical qualifier and description values
are HTML-normalized plain text per lead decision C-8, while
`extras.snapgene` keeps the raw HTML.

The gate is `cargo test -p sequon-conformance --test snapgene_goldens`:

- re-imports every successful fixture and byte-compares the golden;
- re-runs record validation and digest verification;
- validates every golden against `schemas/sequon-record-1.schema.json` and
  parses it back into a valid record;
- asserts every failing fixture returns its documented typed error code and has
  no golden;
- asserts the type-1 twin (002) decodes to the same sequence as the type-0
  golden (001).

Golden regeneration is deliberate and never runs in CI:

```text
SEQUON_REGEN_SNAPGENE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p sequon-conformance \
  --test snapgene_goldens regenerate_goldens -- --ignored
```

Regeneration is ignored by default and gated on that variable. Review the diff
before committing; a success fixture that stops importing, or a failing fixture
whose code changes, is a parser bug to escalate rather than a golden to accept.

## 7. Digest test vectors

`tests/digest-vectors.json` (repository root, per plan sections 2.3.4 and 7.4;
settled as T5) is owned by the contract role and consumed as conformance data. The harness
counts it in CI; it does not implement the digest math.

Required coverage:

| Category | What it proves |
| --- | --- |
| linear forward vs revcomp | `canonical` collapses a linear molecule and its reverse complement; `sequence` stays direction-sensitive |
| circular rotation | a rotated circular input keeps the same `canonical` digest but changes `sequence` |
| circular revcomp rotation | reversed+complemented+rotated circular input keeps the same `canonical` digest |
| N and IUPAC characters | normalization is uppercase/strip-whitespace only; ambiguous letters are preserved, not guessed |

Vector requirements:

- at least four groups for linear and four for circular inputs (plan section
  4.5);
- each entry records `id`, `topology`, `sequence`, expected `sequence` and
  `canonical` digests, and a one-line rationale;
- both digest fields are asserted; the algorithm id is asserted exactly as
  `sequon-digest/1`;
- negative expectations are explicit (rotation/revcomp must *not* change
  `canonical` and *must* change `sequence` where applicable);
- changing a vector or expected digest requires a semantic note; the algorithm
  id changes only for a real semantic change.

## 8. SnapGene external ground truth (manual, local-only)

Purpose: compare the in-repository `.dna` reader against the vendor's own
GenBank export without redistributing vendor output. Per open question Q8,
every input and output of this procedure stays in `testdata/paired/` and is
never committed.

### 8.1 Prerequisites

- A locally licensed SnapGene installation. The exact version string is
  recorded; "latest" is not a version.
- An input `.dna` we are allowed to use: synthetic/self-built is preferred;
  a user-owned, de-identified file is acceptable locally. Never a third-party
  map whose licence is unclear.
- The input must already have a committed counterpart or a planned matrix row,
  so the comparison covers a known case.

### 8.2 Procedure

1. Place the input at `testdata/paired/<stem>.dna`.
2. Open it in SnapGene and confirm the displayed length and topology match the
   fixture manifest. Record a mismatch instead of proceeding silently.
3. `File -> Save As -> GenBank`, saving `testdata/paired/<stem>.gb`. Do not
   edit either file afterwards.
4. Record in `testdata/paired/manifest.local.md` (local-only):
   SnapGene version, OS, date, `<stem>`, and sha256 of both files.
5. Run the comparison command (deliverable C9, available from M5):
   `cargo run -p sequon-conformance -- compare --dna testdata/paired/<stem>.dna --gb testdata/paired/<stem>.gb --out target/conformance/<stem>.json`.
   Until that binary exists, perform the comparison manually and record the
   same facts.
6. Classify every difference in the register (section 9) and attach the report
   to the milestone record.

A paired file that fails to import is a hard comparison failure, not a skipped
row. Paired files are never copied into `testdata/genbank/` or
`testdata/snapgene/`.

### 8.3 Thresholds (plan section 7.5)

| Dimension | Threshold | Comparison rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sequence | 100% | equal after normalization: uppercase, remove whitespace and digits, keep ambiguous IUPAC letters; one base difference fails |
| topology | 100% | `linear`/`circular` must match |
| features | Jaccard >= 99% | tuple `(key, start, end, strand)` after one 0-based half-open normalization; `start` = first segment start, `end` = last segment end; keys compared as written |
| qualifiers | exact modulo documented normalization | only outer quote removal, quote-escape reversal, line unfolding/whitespace collapse and case-only value differences are allowed; everything else is a difference |
| primers | 100% | every SnapGene primer appears as a `primer_bind` feature with matching name and binding site |

**Pass/fail definition (lead decision, T6):** the primary feature comparison
is the coarse tuple above: `key`, the start of the first normalized segment,
the end of the last normalized segment, and strand. A segment-set comparison
is reported as an informational secondary metric and is not a gate. Passing
thresholds is necessary but not sufficient: an explained difference can still
be a parser defect.

## 9. Known-differences register

Every difference found by the comparison, or by inspection while building a
fixture, is recorded here. A row is not optional for a known difference: an
unrecorded difference is treated as unexplained.

| ID | Fixture | Field / path | Canonical value | SnapGene value | Category | Explanation | Decision | Owner | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `KD-001` | `<fixture>` | `<canonical path>` | `<value>` | `<value>` | `<category>` | `<why>` | `<accepted / fixed / escalated>` | `<role>` | open |

Category vocabulary (use one; do not invent new ones without lead approval):

- `NORMALIZATION` - documented formatting normalization (quotes, folding,
  case, whitespace) with no semantic loss.
- `VENDOR_METADATA` - data SnapGene writes that our model deliberately keeps
  in `extras` or does not model.
- `MODEL_LIMIT` - the canonical model cannot represent the item; it must be
  reported in `dropped`/`preserved`, not silently lost.
- `COORDINATE_CONVENTION` - documented 1-based closed to 0-based half-open
  conversion, with a worked example.
- `PARSER_DEFECT` - our reader is wrong; fix before the gate.
- `GROUND_TRUTH_DEFECT` - the vendor export is wrong or misleading; document
  and escalate to lead.
- `OPEN` - cause not yet understood; blocks the gate.

Status values: `open`, `resolved` (fix or explanation landed), `accepted`
(lead signs off that the difference is intentional and harmless). Only the
lead can mark a row `accepted`.

### 9.1 Summary block (filled at M5)

```text
paired fixtures compared:  <n>
sequence match:            <n>/<n> (100%)
topology match:            <n>/<n> (100%)
feature Jaccard:           <min>..<max> (threshold 99%)
qualifier differences:     <n>, all in categories <...>
primers:                   <n>/<n> as primer_bind (100%)
rows by category:          NORMALIZATION <n>, VENDOR_METADATA <n>, ...
open rows:                 <n>
```

### 9.2 Blocking rule

Unexplained differences **block milestone sign-off**. Plan section 7.5 fails
M4 when a difference is unexplained; M5 cannot be signed off while any row is
`open`, any `PARSER_DEFECT` lacks a fix, or any difference lacks a category
and explanation. Meeting the numeric thresholds does not override this rule.

## 10. Adding or changing a fixture

1. Confirm the row exists in section 5; otherwise add it with lead approval
   (and, if it changes the matrix, ask the lead to update plan section 7).
2. Build the fixture from synthetic/self-built input; record origin and
   generator. For a `.dna` fixture, add or edit the entry in
   `crates/sequon-conformance/src/snapgene_fixtures.rs` and regenerate with
   `cargo run -p sequon-conformance --bin gen-snapgene-fixtures`; never hand-edit
   fixture bytes.
3. Compute and record sha256; keep the file byte-stable afterwards.
4. Generate the golden(s) from the importer and review the diff by hand; no
   auto-accept. Single-record fixtures use `<fixture-stem>.json`;
   multi-record fixtures use one `<fixture-stem>.<record-index>.json` per
   record (T3). Do not create report goldens (T4). For SnapGene fixtures run
   the deliberate regeneration test in section 6.4, then run the gate.
5. Assert the full expected outcome: success fields, or error code plus
   position, or warning code plus usable record.
6. Extend determinism checks (section 6.3) to the new fixture.
7. Confirm English-only text, no secrets, no personal data, no machine paths.
8. Respect the size budget: only `150-large-1mb.gb` is allowed to be large;
   the LZMA-limit fixture stays tiny because it exercises the declared-size
   header pre-check rather than a decoded bomb.
9. Update status, counts, coverage-gap section and known differences in this
   file in the same change.

## 12. Tooling versions (verified)

Verified on 2026-10-21 with cargo 1.97.1 (`cargo info <crate> --registry crates-io`); the Python validator is installed by CI (2026-10-22):

| Crate | Version | Licence | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `serde_json` | 1.0.154 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | JSON parsing for the validation harness |
| `jsonschema` (Python) | >=4.23 | MIT | JSON Schema validation runs in `tools/validate_contract.py` (CI installs it). No Rust dev-dependency: that keeps the `jsonschema -> getrandom -> r-efi` LGPL chain out of `Cargo.lock`. |
| `sha2` | 0.10.9 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | fixture determinism gate: sha256 of rebuilt and committed bytes |
| `lzma-rs` | 0.3.0 | MIT | history payload compression for fixtures 011/080; exact pin, default features off; used only by the dev-only conformance crate |

The conformance crate is a development-only package (`publish = false`) and is
not part of the runtime dependency tree. `sequon-io` (features `genbank` and
`snapgene`), `sequon-model` and `sequon-algo` are **dev-dependencies** here:
goldens are produced and re-checked by the committed reader, but no runtime
crate depends on this harness. Its schema tests run with
`cargo test -p sequon-conformance`; they compile both schemas, validate every
`schemas/examples/*.json` document and exercise the negative cases listed in
the test module. The fixture gate
`cargo test -p sequon-conformance --test snapgene_fixtures` rebuilds every
committed `.dna` file, compares bytes and sha256, and walks the container
independently. Digest vectors, goldens and fixtures are data only; no fixture
tool may become a runtime dependency.

sha256 values are recorded with `sha256sum` (Linux) or `shasum -a 256`
(macOS). Any tool that edits fixture bytes must record its version here when
first used.
